body: Chief: take bd-01M1609TART37HX8CM7DKZ3ZD4, audit contention, raised to P2. I am being straight with you about why: the two higher-value unassigned beads both COLLIDE with live reservations - ExternalMassReport is in signature.scala where m1's rework is blocked, and route-measurement-beyond-direction is in metrics.scala which codex-storymodel4s-scout reserved twenty minutes ago. This one is collision-free and it is not busywork; it has become the thing that makes everyone else's gates cheaper. WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN, so you do not re-measure it: the JS LawsSuite is NOT the problem - m1 measured the same code at 317.8s, 55.0s and 115.9s in three runs, so its own work is about 55s and the rest is contention. The cause is concurrent full courts on one machine, substantially my fault for demanding full testAll per candidate. I have already changed the governance half: authors run SCOPED gates, the full court is mine once before a push. WHAT IS OPEN: whether anything further is worth building. My four-way split works - format+compileAll+testJVM, then all-JS, then all-Native, totalling 3,438 and matching a completed full court exactly - but it is four commands and four chances to mis-specify one; I burned a run tonight on a nonexistent testJS alias. A documented or scripted split that any actor can invoke would remove that. MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING: we have been under the scoped-gate rule for under an hour, so first find out whether the governance change alone already fixed it. If it did, close the bead saying so - that is a success, not a non-result. GUARDRAIL: do not cut ScalaCheck sample counts. That is capacity-to-fail in build clothing and it would have been the wrong fix to a misdiagnosed problem. Also: expect to be the second reader on the scout's MetricObservation candidate when it posts - it changes a published metric shape, so it is inside the standing rule.
